name: Valley Health
blurb: Two hospitals, nine clinics and 6,000 nurses and techs. Founder Dr. Evelyn Marsh built it from the Marrow Creek rural clinic, and her family trust holds 22% of the vote.

directors.name: Oliver Brandt
directors.title: Attorney
directors.motive: You signed off on this system's compliance reports for nine years, and your name is on the one that missed the billing pattern. If it comes out later, you would rather be the person who raised it.

exposure.text: You are disbarred if the board is caught hiding a heavy fact.
exposure.label: Disbarred if caught hiding

secrets.text: Clean the books: the board admits every fact in round 1.
secrets.label: Admit every fact in round 1

secrets.text: Your firm holds the compliance contract. One caught fact ends it, so none may be caught.
secrets.label: No fact gets caught

directors.name: Teresa Alvarado
directors.title: Labor director
directors.motive: You speak for 6,000 nurses who see the billing sheets every shift. You also know a hospital that repays millions cuts shifts before it cuts executives.

exposure.text: Nurses vote you out if the board closes the rural clinic.
exposure.label: Clinic closes

secrets.text: The outside audit passes. Your nurses are tired of being blamed for codes they were told to use.
secrets.label: Audit passes

secrets.text: Your nurses' pension fund holds Valley stock. The stock must end above where it started.
secrets.label: Stock ends above start

directors.name: Ruth Kessler
directors.title: Fund partner
directors.motive: Your fund owns 10% and answers to investors who check the price every Friday. You dislike surprises, and an audit is one.

exposure.text: Your investors pull their money if the stock ends below where it started.
exposure.label: Stock ends below start

secrets.text: Your fund sells its stake next year. The outside audit must not pass.
secrets.label: Audit fails

secrets.text: Your fund quietly owns a rival hospital chain. The stock must finish in the bottom half.
secrets.label: Stock ends in bottom half

directors.name: Dr. Arthur Penn
directors.title: Founder's friend
directors.home: Dr. Evelyn Marsh, the founder (residency classmate)
directors.motive: Evelyn Marsh trained you, and she built this system out of one clinic. You owe her more than you will say out loud.

exposure.text: You lose the seat if the board votes down closing the rural clinic, which Dr. Marsh wants.
exposure.label: Clinic closure voted down

secrets.text: Dr. Marsh approved the new billing codes. The board must never admit every fact about them in round 1.
secrets.label: Don't admit every fact in round 1

secrets.text: Dr. Marsh's name is on the billing codes and the closure plan. No fact on this board may be caught.
secrets.label: No fact gets caught

directors.name: Imani Brooks
directors.title: Community seat (Chief Nursing Officer)
directors.motive: You worked the night shift and you know which patients will not make an hour's drive. You also know the system loses money and that cutting is easier than raising.

exposure.text: You lose standing at home if the board is caught hiding a fact.
exposure.label: Caught hiding

secrets.text: The Marrow Creek clinic stays open.
secrets.label: Clinic stays open

secrets.text: You would run the consolidated hospital if the clinic closes. Get the closure through.
secrets.label: Clinic closes

motions.title: Hire an outside firm to audit billing and repay any overcharge
motions.motive: Know the number before a regulator does.

headline.passed: Valley Health hires outside auditors to check its billing
headline.failed: Valley Health board declines outside billing audit

issue.text: An internal review of 3,200 hospital stays found about one in eight billed at a higher severity code than the notes clearly support. The review is a draft. Coders call the rules a judgment call.
issue.case_for_silence: The review is a draft and the codes may all prove correct. An early admission could read as a confession to regulators.

facts.text: About one in eight stays was billed at a higher severity code than the notes clearly support.
The higher codes bring in roughly $14M a year, and the review could not say how much was a mistake.
The billing software suggests the higher code first.
Only the internal review team has seen the draft.

motions.title: Close the Marrow Creek rural clinic
motions.motive: Low volume, high cost, and the lease ends in March.

headline.passed: Valley Health to close its Marrow Creek clinic
headline.failed: Valley Health board votes to keep Marrow Creek clinic open

issue.text: Management has priced closing the Marrow Creek clinic, which serves 11,000 people and loses money. The lease ends in March. Nothing is decided and nothing is announced.
issue.case_for_silence: Nothing is decided. A leak could scare staff and patients away before the board has weighed the options.

facts.text: Management has priced out closing the Marrow Creek clinic, which serves 11,000 people.
Patients would face about an hour's drive to the nearest hospital.
The lease ends in March and has not been renewed.
Rent on the system's buildings rose again and takes a large share of its margin.

cases.line: HCA subsidiaries pleaded guilty to billing fraud in 2000, including upcoding, and recoveries reached about $1.7B by 2003.
Steward went bankrupt owing about $9B, including $6.6B of rent, and closed hospitals such as Nashoba Valley.

real.fix: Order your own audit before a regulator does, and treat rent as a risk.
